message.content: {"mechanism_id":"F_memory_rank_floor","target_component":"F memory update (Lehmer mean) in L-SHADE","observed_evidence":{"task_id":"TASK-03","trace_path":"diagnostic_trace_summary","function":"F11","seed":11,"metric":"F_mean","observed_value":0.08},"causal_hypothesis":"Lehmer mean is dominated by small successful F values because weights=|delta_f| are similar across scales; repeated small-F successes drive M_F toward zero even when population diversity is healthy (0.175), so differential vectors shrink.","algorithmic_change":"Replace the plain Lehmer mean for M_F with a rank-weighted Lehmer mean that down-weights the smallest F samples, plus a per-generation F floor tied to current population spread (not a fixed constant).","mathematical_rule":"w_k = |delta_f_k| * (rank_k / N_succ); M_F = sum(w_k * F_k^2) / sum(w_k * F_k); F_floor = 0.1 * (std(pop)/mean_range); F_used = max(F_sampled, F_floor)","expected_effect":"Keeps M_F in 0.3-0.6 range on F4/F11/F15 while preserving adaptive response; prevents differential vector vanishing without hard-coding a constant floor.","failure_prediction":"On unimodal functions where small F is genuinely optimal, the rank weighting may slow late-stage convergence, raising final error slightly.","ablation_plan":"Compare (a) baseline Lehmer, (b) rank-weighted Lehmer only, (c) spread-scaled floor only, (d) both, across F4/F11/F15 seeds 1-15; report F_mean trajectory and final error.","nearest_known_methods":"Lehmer mean F adaptation (SHADE/L-SHADE), weighted memory updates, dynamic F lower bounds in jSO-style variants.","implementation_requirements":"Track rank of each successful F by magnitude; compute population std each generation; modify M_F update line and F sampling clamp in lshade_canonical.py; no extra memory beyond one scalar."}
